header: THE REPLY OF /api/people-events (step 65a). I keep it apart from the route so it can be tested. The lists are public like the rest of the home page (a name, a post, a department, a photo); no date of birth and no date of joining ever leaves the server. A missing column (sql/14 not yet run) gets a reply that NAMES the fix; any other failure stays generic, so no detail is leaked.

symbols.name: handlePeopleEvents
symbols.sig: export async function handlePeopleEvents(query: QueryFn, now: DateTime = DateTime.now()): Promise<ApiReply>

behaviours: a normal day: 200 with the three lists, the day, the month and the end of the month
the retirement card says the farewell day (the last day of the month), the jubilee card the day the 25th year is completed
a photo address that is not a web address is dropped (null), a web address is kept
a card holds the person and the one day to show, and nothing of the placeholder marker; the reply has no 'sample' flag
no date of birth and no date of joining is in the reply
the query is given the day in India as plain values, never put into the text of the SQL (no injection by construction)
a day with nobody: 200 and three empty lists
the migration not yet run: 503 with the sentence that NAMES the fix
...also in the form TypeORM raises it (driverError)
any other failure: 500, a generic sentence, nothing of the message leaked
a missing column of ANOTHER table is not mistaken for the migration
a failing query becomes that reply, never an exception
the route is never cached (force-dynamic, no-store) and takes no input from the request (no query string, no body, no ticket)
the route reads with the application's own connection, never the AI search's read-only role
there is no production switch for placeholder dates any more (a development database: what the lists show is not a concern)
